description:
Am I done? The stop condition for a coding loop. **Free — no
subscription, no token budget, no rate limit.**

Composes what verifAIed already knows about a branch — failing tests
plus the coverage of the functions you changed — into a single verdict
you can gate on:

  - ``done`` (bool): ``true`` only when there are no gaps at all. This
    is the strict signal to stop.
  - ``status``: ``"done"`` | ``"done-with-warnings"`` | ``"not-done"``.
    ``done-with-warnings`` means the only remaining gaps are ones the
    repo owner marked non-blocking — read this yourself if you want to
    stop early.
  - ``scope``: ``"changed-functions"`` when a default-branch base
    exists (only added/modified functions are judged), else
    ``"all-functions"``.
  - ``gaps``: each remaining problem with a ``ref``, the id to act on
    (``function_id``/``test_id``), and a ``next_action`` pointing at
    ``get_baseline_prompt`` (free) or ``fix_branch`` (paid). Gap kinds:

      - ``failing_test`` — a test that failed or errored.
      - ``untested_function`` / ``partial_function`` — a changed
        function with no coverage, or only some.
      - ``unexercised_browser`` — a changed function that no browser
        reached, in either the browser-coverage or the manual
        dimension. Only judged once one of them exists.
      - ``visually_unreviewed`` — a changed component nobody has
        looked at. ``intent_mismatch`` — somebody looked and it
        didn't do what the change claimed. Both only judged once the
        branch has at least one ``verify_ui`` verdict.
      - ``unverified_recorded_test`` — a recorded test this branch
        has never run, or whose last run failed. Re-run it with
        ``verifaied test run "<feature path>/<name>"`` — the feature
        path is optional and may nest. Branch-wide, not
        diff-scoped. Absent entirely for a repo with no recorded
        tests.
      - ``visual_defect`` — something ``verifaied audit`` measured in
        the rendered page (overflow, contrast, a broken image, a
        console error), from the most recent audit of the branch.
        **The one kind that is a warning by default**, so it routes to
        ``done-with-warnings`` rather than blocking unless the repo
        owner turned it on. Only judged once the branch has been
        audited at least once.

    Gaps are ordered so a component's own
    gaps are immediately followed by its handlers' and render
    branches'; a sub-unit gap carries ``parent_ref`` (the parent's
    ``file::Name``) so you can group or indent them without parsing
    refs. The clustering is presentation only — every gap is still
    individually actionable by its own ``ref`` / ``function_id``.
  - ``not_checked``: signals that couldn't be evaluated (e.g. failing
    tests when no junit.xml was uploaded, or ``unexercised_browser``
    when functions exist but no browser coverage was uploaded) —
    surfaced so a green verdict is never silently green.

Pagination: ``gaps`` is capped at ``max_gaps`` per call (default 50) to
stay within tool-result limits — a low-coverage branch can have hundreds.
``done``, ``status``, ``scope`` and ``gaps_total`` ALWAYS reflect the full
gap set, never just the returned page, so a truncated page is never
mistaken for a clean branch. When more gaps remain, ``has_more`` is
``true``, ``next_offset`` is the offset to pass next, and ``note`` spells
out how to fetch the rest — call again with that ``offset`` until
``has_more`` is ``false``.

The intended loop: run your tests with coverage (pytest → coverage.json,
or ``vitest run --coverage --coverage.provider=istanbul`` →
coverage/coverage-final.json) → ``upload_local_coverage`` →
``check_done`` → fix each gap (``get_baseline_prompt`` / ``fix_branch``)
→ re-upload → repeat until ``done`` is ``true``.

``repository`` is the GitHub 'owner/repo' (a repo UUID also works);
``branch`` defaults to the repository's default branch. Errors with an
actionable message when no analysis exists for the branch yet — upload
coverage first.
name: check_done
